  2) Month 3 onward: convert to full 32-GPU reserved pool.

- Pricing (reserved per-hour):

  • Burst (on-demand) blended safeguard rate: $1.80 / GPU-hour (applies only to auto-burst hours, capped).

- Throughput / SLA guardrails: 95th percentile P99 latency target for seq512 text gen: <= 120ms, baseline sustained throughput guarantee: 6,000 tokens/sec. Burst headroom up to ~9,000 tokens/sec for up to 72 hours in events. Full SLA details attached.

Next steps: please review the attached proposal and SLA. If this looks OK I can send a procurement-ready summary and DocuSign link (price + PO instructions).

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you want to walk through the numbers.

Best,

Hi Marcus / Tessa —

Quick technical note on the burst buffer and throttling behavior so procurement has the right expectations:

- Burst buffer behavior: when traffic exceeds reserved pool capacity, we spin up prewarmed burst instances tied to the customer's account. Those instances are metered at the burst rate and subject to the monthly cap (2,000 GPU-hours in the transition).
- Auto-throttle: after the cap is hit, requests will be routed to the most cost-efficient compatible model variant (quantized variant) with graceful degradation logic. That fallback preserves token throughput but may increase latency by ~15–40ms depending on prompt shape.
- Overlap billing: during the migration window we bill each cluster for the hours used. To minimize duplicate costs, we recommend keystone cutovers during low-traffic windows and use prefix caching to avoid full cold starts.
- Metrics: we record per-route token吞吐 (tokens/sec) and per-request KV cache hit rates; those metrics are exposed in the Console for 90 days by default (longer retention available as an add-on).

Happy to provide a short run-book for your SREs for a dry-run migration.

—Dev
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference
